notice: Three verified staged archives were uploaded to a Canadian-region S3 bucket with Object Lock and versioning enabled. Upload and remote byte/checksum verification are complete. No Object Lock retention has been applied, so these objects are NOT yet immutable and NOT remote-verified under docs/IMMUTABLE_STORAGE_CONTRACT.md. They remain non-production and are not admitted to transformation or ingestion.

region.evidenceReference: aws s3api get-bucket-location returned LocationConstraint=ca-central-1 on 2026-08-12

verificationMethod: Byte length and checksum were read back from S3 with head-object --checksum-mode ENABLED after upload. get-object-attributes is not available to the current principal (AccessDenied on s3:GetObjectAttributes), so head-object is the remote evidence source.

entries.checksumNote: This object was uploaded as a 1187-part multipart upload, so S3 stores a composite SHA-256 (a SHA-256 over the concatenated per-part SHA-256 digests), not a whole-object SHA-256. S3 cannot return a FULL_OBJECT SHA-256 for a multipart upload; full-object checksums are supported only for CRC32, CRC32C and CRC64NVME. The composite value therefore cannot equal the staged whole-file SHA-256 and no direct remote comparison to it is possible.

independentIntegrityProof.method: Recomputed the composite SHA-256 locally from the staged file using the same 8388608-byte part size and compared it to the value S3 returned.
independentIntegrityProof.conclusion: The stored object is byte-for-byte identical to the staged file whose whole-file SHA-256 is 80c37461f4deccfdfffc26124e9064d53a94dde660b9f96194445870393af130. Integrity is established, but not by a direct S3-side whole-object SHA-256.

canadianRegionEvidence.detail: Bucket location constraint ca-central-1 confirmed remotely.

remoteByteLengthMatch.detail: All three objects returned a remote ContentLength equal to the staged byte length.

remoteChecksum.detail: Québec and Alberta return a FULL_OBJECT SHA-256 that matches the staged checksum exactly. The NRCan canopy object returns only a composite multipart SHA-256, which cannot be compared directly to the staged whole-file SHA-256. Its integrity is established by an independent local recomputation of the composite rather than by an S3-side whole-object SHA-256.

providerVersionIdPayload.detail: A version ID was returned and read back for each of the three payload objects.

providerVersionIdSidecar.detail: No manifest.json sidecar object was uploaded, so no manifestVersionId exists. The contract requires separate provider version IDs for payload and sidecar.

activeComplianceRetention.detail: No Object Lock retention has been applied to any object version. The bucket has Object Lock enabled but no default retention, which is intentional.

reviewerAndReviewTime.detail: No accountable human reviewer has recorded a review of this promotion.

openDecisions: The object keys used here follow a flat raw/<source-id>/<retrieved-date>/<filename> layout. This does NOT match the canonical snapshot layout that lib/archive-staging/validate.ts derives, which is raw/{sourceId}/{sourceVersion}/{retrievedAt}/{sha256}/payload/{lowercase-filename} plus a sibling manifest.json. A promotion manifest built from these keys would be rejected by validatePromotionManifest. The key layout must be settled before any retention is applied, because compliance-mode retention cannot be shortened or removed by anyone, including the account root, and would permanently pin these objects at non-canonical keys.
No manifest.json sidecar has been written or uploaded for any of the three snapshots.
Retention duration and mode remain unapplied. Any retention decision should be applied per object version, never as a bucket default, so that future test objects and mistakes are not silently locked.
An accountable reviewer must be named before any promotion can be recorded as remote-verified.
